function.name: religion_history_get_councils
function.description: Retrieves a list of major councils in a specified religion. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

religion.description: Name of the religion for which to retrieve the councils.

count.description: Number of top councils to retrieve.

function.name: religion_history_get_reformations
function.description: Retrieves a list of major reformations in a specified religion. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

function.name: religion_history_get_schisms
function.description: Retrieves a list of major schisms in a specified religion. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

count.description: Number of top schisms to retrieve.

message.content:
The “three great schisms” in Christian history are usually understood to be:

| # | Schism | Approximate Date | Key Parties & Outcome |
|---|--------|------------------|-----------------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism (East–West Schism)** | 1054 CE | Separation of the Eastern Orthodox Church from the Roman Catholic Church; formalized by mutual excommunications of the Patriarch of Constantinople and the Pope. |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 CE | Break from the Roman Catholic Church led by figures such as Martin Luther, John Calvin, and others; resulted in the creation of Lutheran, Reformed, Anglican, and other Protestant denominations. |
| 3 | **East–West Schism (Second Great Schism)** | 1965 CE | Often referred to as the “Second Great Schism” or “Modern Schism,” it marks the formal split between the Eastern Orthodox Church and the Oriental Orthodox Churches (e.g., Coptic, Armenian, Syriac). |

These three events are considered the most significant ruptures in the unity of Christianity, each reshaping the religious, cultural, and political landscapes of their times.
